questions.q: Marginal cost cuts average total cost:
options: At the highest point of ATC
At the lowest point of ATC
questions.why: If MC is below ATC, ATC falls. If MC is above it, ATC rises. So they meet at the minimum.

questions.q: What causes the short-run ATC curve to rise at high output?
questions.why: With a fixed factor, each extra unit takes more labour.

questions.q: Wages rise 10% and output per worker rises 20%. What happens to labour cost per unit?
questions.why: Productivity rose faster than wages, so each unit takes less labour cost.

questions.q: A sharp rise in wages is most likely to lead firms to:
options: Raise fixed costs by buying nothing
questions.why: Capital becomes relatively cheaper, so firms switch towards it.

questions.q: Explain why a rise in rent would raise a firm's average total cost but not its marginal cost.

ideas.label: Rent is a fixed cost, so it adds to total and average cost
Marginal cost is the extra cost of one more unit, and rent doesn't change with output

questions.model: Rent is a fixed cost, so it adds to total and average cost. Marginal cost is the extra cost of one more unit, and rent does not change with output, so marginal cost stays the same.
questions.why: MC only picks up costs that change with output.

tests.answer: Rent is a fixed cost so ATC rises, but MC is the extra cost of one more unit, which is unaffected.
